title: Preserve signal strides when constructing zero-copy frames
body:
## Problem
`to_frames` derives both output strides from `x.itemsize`, assuming contiguous input. For a subsampled or reversed signal view, the resulting frames read different samples from the requested logical signal and can point outside that view.

## Change
Use the input's actual one-dimensional sample stride for both frame and hop strides. The returned frames remain zero-copy views, with the existing writeability behavior.

## Validation
- The 12 new tests against unchanged upstream: 8 failed, 4 passed.
- New tests plus the existing framing test: 13 passed on Python 3.9.25.
- Slicing-based expected windows cover contiguous, subsampled and reversed views, two hop sizes, both writeability settings, shared storage and mutation aliasing.
- The reversed-input fixture is placed inside a larger owned buffer, so the old implementation can be tested without reading outside the allocation.
- Independent read-only review found no blockers.
